                  for a in (1, 4) for b in range(5)]
C5: List[Perm] = [tuple((x + b) % 5 for x in range(5)) for b in range(5)]


def densities(box: List[Perm]) -> Dict[CycleType, float]:
    counts: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
    for p in box:
        counts[cycle_type(p)] = counts.get(cycle_type(p), 0) + 1
    return {t: c / len(box) for t, c in counts.items()}


def entropy(dist: Dict[CycleType, float]) -> float:
    return -sum(q * log2(q) for q in dist.values() if q > 0)

def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i:: i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i:: i]))
    return [i for i in range(2, n + 1) if sieve[i]]


Poly = List[int]


def _trim(a: Poly) -> Poly:
    while a and a[-1] == 0:
        a.pop()
    return a


def _mul(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    if not a or not b:
        return []
    out = [0] * (len(a) + len(b) - 1)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        if ai:
            for j, bj in enumerate(b):
                out[i + j] = (out[i + j] + ai * bj) % p
    return _trim(out)


def _divmod(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Tuple[Poly, Poly]:
    a, db = a[:], len(b) - 1
    inv = pow(b[-1], p - 2, p)
    q = [0] * max(0, len(a) - db)
    while a and len(a) - 1 >= db:
        shift = len(a) - 1 - db
        c = (a[-1] * inv) % p
        q[shift] = c
        for i, bi in enumerate(b):
            a[shift + i] = (a[shift + i] - c * bi) % p
        _trim(a)
    return _trim(q), a


def _gcd(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a, b = _trim(a[:]), _trim(b[:])
    while b:
        a, b = b, _divmod(a, b, p)[1]
    if a:
        inv = pow(a[-1], p - 2, p)
        a = [(c * inv) % p for c in a]
    return a


def _powmod(base: Poly, e: int, mod: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    r: Poly = [1]
    b = _divmod(base, mod, p)[1]
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            r = _divmod(_mul(r, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        b = _divmod(_mul(b, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        e >>= 1
    return r


def _sub(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    n = max(len(a), len(b))
    return _trim([((a[i] if i < len(a) else 0) - (b[i] if i < len(b) else 0)) % p
                  for i in range(n)])


def factorisation_type(f: Poly, p: int):
    f = _trim([c % p for c in f])
    df = _trim([(i * f[i]) % p for i in range(1, len(f))])
    if not df or len(_gcd(f, df, p)) > 1:
        return None
    degrees: List[int] = []
    h: Poly = [0, 1]
    g, d = f[:], 0
    while len(g) - 1 > 0 and d < len(f):
        d += 1
        h = _powmod(h, p, g, p)
        gd = _gcd(g, _sub(h, [0, 1], p), p)
        if len(gd) - 1 > 0:
            degrees.extend([d] * ((len(gd) - 1) // d))
            g = _divmod(g, gd, p)[0]
            if len(g) - 1 > 0:
                h = _divmod(h, g, p)[1]
    if len(g) - 1 > 0:
        degrees.append(len(g) - 1)
    return tuple(sorted(degrees))


def observed(f: Poly, limit: int = 30000) -> Dict[CycleType, float]:
    counts: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
    total = 0
    for p in primes_up_to(limit):
        t = factorisation_type(f, p)
        if t is not None and sum(t) == 5:
            counts[t] = counts.get(t, 0) + 1
            total += 1
    return {t: c / total for t, c in counts.items()}

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>The Splitting-Type Channel Explorer</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    Pick a Galois group for a quintic polynomial. Everything below is computed by exact enumeration
    of that group: how much information the factorisation type of a prime carries, how much of it a
    congruence condition is allowed to hear, and what happens when several primes are multiplied
    together.
  </p>

  <div class="panel">
    <div class="row">
      <div>
        <label for="grp">Galois group of the quintic</label>
        <select id="grp">
          <option value="C5">C₅ — cyclic, order 5 (abelian)</option>
          <option value="D5">D₅ — dihedral, order 10</option>
          <option value="F20">F₂₀ = AGL(1,5) — order 20</option>
          <option value="A5">A₅ — alternating, order 60 (perfect)</option>
          <option value="S5" selected>S₅ — symmetric, order 120</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <div>
        <label for="dial">Dial (what a residue class reads)</label>
        <select id="dial">
          <option value="ab" selected>the full abelianization map</option>
          <option value="sign">the sign character (quadratic-residue bit)</option>
          <option value="triv">the trivial dial</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <div>
        <label for="k">Primes combined: k = <span id="klab" class="num">1</span></label>
        <input id="k" type="range" min="1" max="8" value="1" />
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h2>The splitting-type alphabet</h2>
  <div class="panel">
    <table id="tbl">
      <thead><tr><th>factorisation type</th><th>elements</th><th>density</th><th style="width:38%"></th><th>parity</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody></tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <h2>The bit ledger</h2>
  <div class="panel">
    <div class="kpi">
      <div><div class="v num" id="ht">—</div><div class="l">H(T): entropy of the splitting type</div></div>
      <div><div class="v num" id="hd">—</div><div class="l">H(dial): entropy of the dial</div></div>
      <div><div class="v num" id="mi">—</div><div class="l">I(dial ; T): bits transmitted, one prime</div></div>
      <div><div class="v num" id="cap">—</div><div class="l">cap: log₂ of the abelianization order</div></div>
      <div><div class="v num" id="res">—</div><div class="l">H(T | dial): bits locked away</div></div>
      <div><div class="v num" id="mik">—</div><div class="l">bits transmitted over k primes</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="verdict" id="verdict"></div>

    <details>
      <summary>Click to reveal why these numbers are exactly what they are</summary>
      <p>
        By the Chebotarev density theorem the Frobenius element of a random prime is uniformly
        distributed over the Galois group, so the long-run statistics of factorisation types are
        simply conjugacy-class counts. A congruence condition on the prime can read only a
        homomorphism of the group into an abelian group, and every such homomorphism factors through
        the abelianization (the group with all commutators set to one). Hence the cap
        <em>I(dial ; T) ≤ log₂|abelianization|</em>.
      </p>
      <p>
        A homomorphic dial has fibres that are cosets of its kernel, so it is exactly uniform on its
        image: <em>H(dial) = log₂|image|</em>. If in addition the factorisation type
        <em>determines</em> the dial value — which is what “the sign of a permutation is a
        function of its cycle type” says — nothing is lost and
        <em>I(dial ; T) = log₂|image|</em> exactly. For S₅ that is one bit. For the perfect
        group A₅ the image is trivial and the answer is a parameter-free zero. For
        F₂₀ the type does <em>not</em> determine the dial — two dial classes are
        merged inside the type [1,4] — and the transmitted information falls strictly below the
        cap, to 3/2 bits.
      </p>
      <p>
        Slide k upward to combine primes. When the type determines the dial, the k-prime channel
        transmits <em>exactly the same</em> number of bits for every k: there is no almost-prime
        bonus, because the product of k characters is still one character and the image cannot grow.
        When the type does not determine the dial (try F₂₀), combining primes actually
        <em>loses</em> information, decaying towards the merged-coset floor.
      </p>
    </details>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
// ---------- permutations of {0,1,2,3,4} ----------
function permsOf5() {
  const out = [], a = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4];
  (function rec(k) {
    if (k === 5) { out.push(a.slice()); return; }
    for (let i = k; i < 5; i++) {
      [a[k], a[i]] = [a[i], a[k]];
      rec(k + 1);
      [a[k], a[i]] = [a[i], a[k]];
    }
  })(0);
  return out;
}
const ALL = permsOf5();
const key = p => p.join("");
const parse = s => s.split("").map(Number);
const compose = (p, q) => q.map(x => p[x]);              // p after q
const inverse = p => { const r = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]; p.forEach((v, i) => { r[v] = i; }); return r; };
const ID = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4];

function cycleType(p) {
  const seen = [false, false, false, false, false], out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    if (!seen[i]) { let l = 0, j = i; while (!seen[j]) { seen[j] = true; j = p[j]; l++; } out.push(l); }
  }
  return out.sort((x, y) => x - y);
}
function signOf(p) { let s = 1; for (const l of cycleType(p)) if (l % 2 === 0) s = -s; return s; }

// ---------- the transitive quintic groups, as subgroups of S5 ----------
const affine = (a, b) => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map(x => (a * x + b) % 5);
function groupOf(name) {
  if (name === "S5") return ALL.slice();
  if (name === "A5") return ALL.filter(p => signOf(p) === 1);
  const units = name === "C5" ? [1] : (name === "D5" ? [1, 4] : [1, 2, 3, 4]);
  const out = [];
  for (const a of units) for (let b = 0; b < 5; b++) out.push(affine(a, b));
  return out;
}

// ---------- derived subgroup, abelianization cosets ----------
function derivedSubgroup(G) {
  const inG = new Set(G.map(key));
  const elems = new Set([key(ID)]);
  for (const x of G) for (const y of G) {
    elems.add(key(compose(compose(x, y), compose(inverse(x), inverse(y)))));
  }
  let changed = true;
  while (changed) {
    changed = false;
    const arr = [...elems].map(parse);
    for (const x of arr) for (const y of arr) {
      const k = key(compose(x, y));
      if (!elems.has(k) && inG.has(k)) { elems.add(k); changed = true; }
    }
  }
  return [...elems].map(parse);
}
function cosetLabeller(D) {
  return x => {
    let best = null;
    for (const d of D) { const k = key(compose(x, d)); if (best === null || k < best) best = k; }
    return best;
  };
}

// ---------- entropy helpers ----------
const entOfMap = d => -[...d.values()].filter(p => p > 0).reduce((s, p) => s + p * Math.log2(p), 0);
function entropyFromCounts(counts) {
  const vals = [...counts.values()].filter(c => c > 0);
  const n = vals.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  return -vals.reduce((s, c) => s + (c / n) * Math.log2(c / n), 0);
}
function tally(G, f) {
  const m = new Map();
  for (const x of G) { const v = f(x); m.set(v, (m.get(v) || 0) + 1); }
  return m;
}
function mutualInfo(G, dial, type) {
  return entropyFromCounts(tally(G, dial)) + entropyFromCounts(tally(G, type))
       - entropyFromCounts(tally(G, x => dial(x) + "|" + type(x)));
}

// ---------- the exact k-prime product channel ----------
// The dial values form a group; the dial of a product of k primes is the product of the k dial
// values, and the read-out is the tuple of the k factorisation types.  Coordinates are
// independent, so the conditional law of the product given the tuple of types is the convolution
// of the per-coordinate conditional laws, and the sum over tuples reduces to a sum over multisets
// weighted by multinomial coefficients.
function productChannelInfo(G, dial, mulLabel, unitLabel, k) {
  const byType = new Map();
  for (const x of G) {
    const t = cycleType(x).join(","), l = dial(x);
    if (!byType.has(t)) byType.set(t, { n: 0, cond: new Map() });
    const e = byType.get(t);
    e.n += 1;
    e.cond.set(l, (e.cond.get(l) || 0) + 1);
  }
  const list = [...byType.values()].map(e => ({
    p: e.n / G.length,
    cond: new Map([...e.cond.entries()].map(([l, c]) => [l, c / e.n]))
  }));
  const refines = list.every(e => e.cond.size === 1);

  const conv = (a, b) => {
    const out = new Map();
    for (const [l1, p1] of a) for (const [l2, p2] of b) {
      const l = mulLabel(l1, l2);
      out.set(l, (out.get(l) || 0) + p1 * p2);
    }
    return out;
  };
  const fact = n => { let f = 1; for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) f *= i; return f; };
  const multinomial = counts => counts.reduce((r, c) => r / fact(c), fact(k));

  const marg = new Map();
  for (const x of G) marg.set(dial(x), (marg.get(dial(x)) || 0) + 1 / G.length);
  let margK = new Map([[unitLabel, 1]]);
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) margK = conv(margK, marg);

  let condH = 0;
  const m = list.length;
  (function walk(i, left, weight, dist, counts) {
    if (i === m - 1) {
      let d = dist;
      for (let j = 0; j < left; j++) d = conv(d, list[i].cond);
      condH += weight * Math.pow(list[i].p, left) * multinomial(counts.concat([left])) * entOfMap(d);
      return;
    }
    for (let c = 0; c <= left; c++) {
      let d = dist;
      for (let j = 0; j < c; j++) d = conv(d, list[i].cond);
      walk(i + 1, left - c, weight * Math.pow(list[i].p, c), d, counts.concat([c]));
    }
  })(0, k, 1, new Map([[unitLabel, 1]]), []);

  return { bits: entOfMap(margK) - condH, refines: refines, imageBits: Math.log2(marg.size) };
}

// ---------- assemble one scenario ----------
function analyse(gname, dname, k) {
  const G = groupOf(gname);
  const D = derivedSubgroup(G);
  const label = cosetLabeller(D);
  const dial = dname === "sign" ? (x => String(signOf(x)))
             : dname === "triv" ? (x => "e")
             : (x => label(x));
  const unit = dname === "sign" ? "1" : (dname === "triv" ? "e" : label(ID));
  const mul = dname === "sign" ? ((a, b) => String(Number(a) * Number(b)))
            : dname === "triv" ? (() => "e")
            : ((a, b) => label(compose(parse(a), parse(b))));
  const type = x => cycleType(x).join(",");

  const counts = tally(G, type);
  const ht = entropyFromCounts(counts);
  const hd = entropyFromCounts(tally(G, dial));
  const mi = mutualInfo(G, dial, type);
  const cap = Math.log2(G.length / D.length);
  const pc = productChannelInfo(G, dial, mul, unit, k);
  return { G: G, counts: counts, ht: ht, hd: hd, mi: mi, cap: cap, res: ht - mi, pc: pc };
}

// ---------- rendering (browser only) ----------
if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
  const render = () => {
    const gname = document.getElementById("grp").value;
    const dname = document.getElementById("dial").value;
    const k = parseInt(document.getElementById("k").value, 10);
    document.getElementById("klab").textContent = k;

    const A = analyse(gname, dname, k);
    const tb = document.querySelector("#tbl tbody");
    tb.innerHTML = "";
    for (const [t, c] of [...A.counts.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1])) {
      const dens = c / A.G.length;
      let par = 1;
      for (const l of t.split(",").map(Number)) if (l % 2 === 0) par = -par;
      const tr = document.createElement("tr");
      tr.innerHTML = '<td class="num">[' + t + ']</td><td class="num">' + c + '</td>' +
        '<td class="num">' + dens.toFixed(4) + '</td>' +
        '<td><div class="bar" style="width:' + (dens * 100).toFixed(1) + '%"></div></td>' +
        '<td>' + (par === 1 ? "even" : "odd") + '</td>';
      tb.appendChild(tr);
    }

    const f = x => (Math.abs(x) < 1e-12 ? "0.0000" : x.toFixed(4));
    document.getElementById("ht").textContent = f(A.ht);
    document.getElementById("hd").textContent = f(A.hd);
    document.getElementById("mi").textContent = f(A.mi);
    document.getElementById("cap").textContent = f(A.cap);
    document.getElementById("res").textContent = f(A.res);
    document.getElementById("mik").textContent = f(A.pc.bits);

    let msg;
    if (A.cap < 1e-12) {
      msg = "<b>Sealed.</b> The group is perfect, so its abelianization is trivial: every dial a " +
            "congruence can read is constant and the transmitted information is exactly zero — " +
            "with " + f(A.ht) + " bits of splitting entropy present and none of it audible, at any k.";
    } else if (A.pc.refines && Math.abs(A.mi - A.cap) < 1e-9) {
      msg = "<b>The cap is attained.</b> The factorisation type determines the dial, so the channel " +
            "transmits the full " + f(A.cap) + " bits — and combining k primes transmits exactly " +
            "the same amount: no almost-prime bonus.";
    } else {
      msg = "<b>Strictly below the cap.</b> The dial could carry " + f(A.cap) + " bits, but the " +
            "factorisation type does not determine it: some type fibre meets two dial classes, so " +
            "only " + f(A.mi) + " bits get through at k = 1, and " + f(A.pc.bits) + " bits at k = " + k + ".";
    }
    document.getElementById("verdict").innerHTML = msg;
  };
  for (const id of ["grp", "dial", "k"]) {
    document.getElementById(id).addEventListener("input", render);
  }
  render();
}

if (typeof module !== "undefined") { module.exports = { analyse: analyse }; }
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    }
  ],
  "interactive_layout": "
# The Splitting-Type Channel: a guided tour

> **The question.** Take a quintic polynomial with integer coefficients and a prime $p$. Modulo $p$
> the polynomial factors into irreducible pieces, and the pattern of their degrees — a partition of
> $5$ — is the **splitting type** of $p$. Now suppose someone tells you only the remainder
> $p \bmod m$. *How many bits have they told you about the splitting type?*

The answer turns out to be an exact number, computable from a finite group, and at degree five it
takes its two extreme values: **exactly one bit**, and **exactly zero**.

---

## 1. Primes become permutations

Attach to the polynomial its **Galois group** $G$: the symmetries of its five roots. Two classical
theorems make the bridge:

- **Dedekind's factorisation theorem** — the splitting type of $p$ is the *cycle type* of the
  Frobenius permutation attached to $p$.
- **Chebotarev's density theorem** — as $p$ ranges over the primes, that permutation is
  *equidistributed* over $G$.

So the infinite, mysterious set of primes may be replaced by a finite, explicit probability space:
the group $G$ with every element equally likely. The long-run statistics of factorisation types are
just conjugacy-class counts. Read more at
[Chebotarev density theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chebotarev%27s_density_theorem) and
[Dedekind's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedekind%27s_theorem_on_the_factorization_of_polynomials).

Let us see the dictionary in action on real primes.

{{algorithm:0}}

Running the census on $x^5 - x - 1$ over the primes below $20000$ reproduces the seven predicted
densities to within a fraction of a percent — and, as a by-product, reports the *ramified* primes
$19$ and $151$, whose product $2869$ is the discriminant of the polynomial. (A widely circulated
value of $-283$ for this discriminant belongs to a quartic; the computation settles the matter.)

---

## 2. Counting the bits

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the entropy formalism used throughout</summary>

For a finite box $S$ with the uniform measure and a read-out $g : S \to B$, write $S_g(a)$ for the
fibre through $a$. The counting entropy is
$$H_S(g) = \log_2 |S| - \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{a \in S} \log_2 |S_g(a)|,$$
which is Shannon's $-\sum_b P(b)\log_2 P(b)$ written so that every element contributes once. For a
second read-out $k$, the conditional entropy $H_S(g \mid k)$ is the average of $H(g)$ over the strata
of $k$, and the mutual information is $I_S(g;k) = H_S(g) - H_S(g\mid k)$.

Three one-line facts do all the work below:

1. a constant read-out has zero entropy, and zero mutual information with everything;
2. if $k$ **refines** $g$ (i.e. $k(x)=k(y) \Rightarrow g(x)=g(y)$) then $I(g;k) = H(g)$;
3. if all fibres of $g$ have the same size $c$, then $H(g) = \log_2(|S|/c)$.

</details>

The symmetric group $S_5$ splits into seven cycle-type classes of sizes $1, 10, 15, 20, 20, 30, 24$.
Feeding those into the entropy formula gives a closed form:
$$H(T) = \frac{7}{5} + \frac{17}{40}\log_2 3 + \frac{5}{24}\log_2 5 = 2.55734\ldots \text{ bits},$$
the **largest splitting entropy of any quintic**. Restricting to the even permutations $A_5$ kills
the three odd types, and four survive with sizes $1, 15, 20, 24$:
$$H(T) = \frac{2}{15} + \frac{7}{20}\log_2 3 + \frac{5}{12}\log_2 5 = 1.65554\ldots \text{ bits}.$$

{{demo:1}}

The same script certifies the decimals by pure integer arithmetic: $2^{1054} < 3^{665}$ pins
$\log_2 3$ from below, $3^{306} < 2^{485}$ from above, and similarly for $\log_2 5$, which sandwiches
$H(T)$ between $2.5573$ and $2.5574$ without ever trusting a floating-point logarithm.

---

## 3. What a congruence is allowed to hear

Here is the conceptual heart. A congruence condition is a *commutative* object: residues multiply,
and order does not matter. By class field theory, the only functions of the Frobenius element that a
residue class can compute are **homomorphisms into abelian groups** — call them **dials**. Every dial
factors through the **abelianization** $G^{\mathrm{ab}} = G/[G,G]$, the group with all commutators
erased. Hence the universal ceiling
$$I(\text{dial} ; T) \;\le\; \log_2 |G^{\mathrm{ab}}|.$$

- For $S_5$, $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has order $2$: the one surviving dial is the sign of the permutation,
  arithmetically the quadratic-residue bit of the discriminant $2869$. **One bit.**
- For $A_5$ — a [perfect group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_group), equal to its own
  commutator subgroup — $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is trivial. **Zero bits.**

Now play with it. The widget below enumerates whichever quintic Galois group you choose, computes its
abelianization from scratch, and reports the whole bit ledger — including what happens when you
combine several primes.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Things worth trying:

- Switch between $S_5$ and $A_5$ and watch $2.5573$ bits collapse to one, and $1.6555$ bits collapse
  to nothing.
- Select $F_{20}$ (the group of order $20$): the ceiling is $2$ bits, but only $1.5$ get through,
  because the type $[1,4]$ is compatible with two different dial values.
- Drag the $k$ slider. For $S_5$ and $A_5$ the answer never moves — *no almost-prime bonus*. For
  $F_{20}$ it decays as $1 + 2^{-k}$: combining primes actually destroys information there.

## 4. The theorems

> **The abelianization law at $S_5$ (sharp form).** For every homomorphism $\varphi$ of $S_5$ into
> any abelian group, $I(\varphi ; T)$ equals $1$ if $\varphi$ is nontrivial and $0$ if it is trivial.
> In particular $I(\mathrm{sign} ; T) = 1$ exactly. There is no intermediate regime.

> **The $A_5$ seal.** Every multiplicative read-out of $A_5$ into an abelian group is *constant*.
> Hence $I(d ; T) = 0$ for every dial $d$ and **every** read-out $T$ — a parameter-free zero.

> **The exact law.** A homomorphic dial is uniform on its image, so $H(\varphi) = \log_2|\mathrm{image}\,\varphi|$;
> and if the read-out refines the dial, $I(\varphi ; T) = \log_2|\mathrm{image}\,\varphi|$ exactly.

> **No almost-prime bonus.** Under the same hypothesis, the $k$-fold product dial transmits
> $\log_2|\mathrm{image}\,\varphi|$ bits for every $k \ge 1$.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the proof of the $A_5$ seal (four lines)</summary>

Let $d : A_5 \to M$ be multiplicative with $M$ abelian. Taking $x = y = 1$ gives $d(1) = 1$, so $d$
is a homomorphism. Its kernel is a normal subgroup of the simple group $A_5$, hence trivial or
everything. If it were trivial, $d$ would embed $A_5$ into an abelian group and $A_5$ would be
commutative — but the three-cycles $(0\,1\,2)$ and $(0\,1\,3)$ do not commute. So the kernel is all
of $A_5$ and $d$ is constant; a constant read-out has zero mutual information with anything. $\square$

</details>

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the proof of the one-bit law at $S_5$</summary>

Let $\varphi : S_5 \to M$ be a homomorphism into an abelian group. Restricted to $A_5$ it is trivial,
by the argument above. Hence if $\mathrm{sign}\,x = \mathrm{sign}\,y$ then $xy^{-1}$ is even and
$\varphi(x) = \varphi(y)$: the dial factors through the sign, and the sign is a function of the cycle
type, so the type refines the dial and $I(\varphi;T) = H(\varphi)$. If $\varphi$ is nontrivial, pick
$\tau$ with $\varphi(\tau) \ne 1$; necessarily $\tau$ is odd, and for $x,y$ of opposite sign,
$xy^{-1}\tau^{-1}$ is even, giving $\varphi(x)\varphi(y)^{-1} = \varphi(\tau) \neq 1$. So the fibres
of $\varphi$ are exactly the two cosets of $A_5$, each of size $60$, and $H(\varphi) = \log_2 2 = 1$.
$\square$

</details>

## 5. Measuring a zero honestly

A theorem says the information is exactly $0$ (at $A_5$) or exactly $1$ (at $S_5$). A finite
experiment will never return those numbers, and the reason is not noise but **bias**: the plug-in
estimator of mutual information over-reports, badly, when the conditioning variable has many classes.
At conductor $2869$ the dial has $2868$ classes and a few thousand primes; sparse coincidences
manufacture a fifth of a bit out of nothing.

{{algorithm:1}}

The fix is a **permutation reference** designed so that the channel the theory predicts survives the
shuffle and only the finer assignment is randomised. In the campaign behind these results the raw
estimate was $1.2157$ bits against a null of $1.2188 \pm 0.0036$ — the observed value sitting *inside*
its own null, $z = -0.85$ — so the entire excess over the theoretical one bit was estimator bias. For
the $A_5$ polynomial, four residue directions ($m = 3, 7, 11, 31$) all landed on their nulls, worst
$|z| = 1.72$, the semiprime channel giving $0.0004$ bits, and no odd type was ever observed.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the ledger of defects that designed checks caught</summary>

1. A dictionary error in root counts for the type $[1,2,2]$: one quadratic pair contributes two roots
   in $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$, not four — caught by a crash at $p = 2$.
2. A discriminant migration: $2869$, not the quartic value $-283$ — caught by repeated factors modulo
   $151$.
3. A sign-encoding inversion, surfacing as an agreement of exactly $0.0000$ instead of $1.0000$: a
   *perfect anti-correlation* is the law confirming itself through a flipped convention.
4. Plug-in bias on the headline quantity itself, $+0.22$ bits at a $2868$-class dial.
5. A null design that permuted labels within strata, thereby deleting the very channel under test.
6. An identifier mismatch that silently collapsed all strata into one, so a "stratified" shuffle was
   in fact global.

The transportable rules: permutation-reference every information estimate at a large conductor; make
your null preserve the predicted channel and randomise only what is finer; and treat an exact $0$ or
$1$ agreement rate as a *fingerprint of correctness*, with anything in between as a bug alarm.

## 7. Where this leaves us

The capacity of the congruence channel is not an empirical quantity but a group-theoretic invariant:
$\log_2$ of the size of the abelianization, attained exactly when the splitting type determines the
character. At degree five the invariant hits both extremes, and neither statement is special to five:
the sign carries exactly one bit in *every* degree, and for $n \ge 5$ the perfect group $A_n$ seals
its channel completely.

There is a practical moral for anyone building statistical models on arithmetic data. Against an
$A_5$ quintic, congruence features are provably worthless — the mutual information is zero, so by the
[data-processing inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_processing_inequality) no model can
beat chance, ever. Against an $S_5$ quintic you get one bit, attained by a single quadratic character,
and anything claiming more is overfitting. Knowing the exact capacity of a channel is the cheapest
possible defence against fooling yourself.

/-- A rational lower bound for `log₂ a` from an integer power inequality. -/
lemma logb_two_lower {a m n : ℕ} (ha : 1 < a) (hn : 0 < n) (h : 2 ^ m < a ^ n) :
    (m : ℝ) / n < Real.logb 2 (a : ℝ) := by
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
  have ha' : (1 : ℝ) < a := by exact_mod_cast ha
  have hlt : ((2 : ℝ)) ^ m < ((a : ℝ)) ^ n := by exact_mod_cast h
  have hlog : Real.log ((2 : ℝ) ^ m) < Real.log ((a : ℝ) ^ n) :=
    Real.log_lt_log (by positivity) hlt
  rw [Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow] at hlog
  have hn' : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  rw [Real.logb, div_lt_div_iff₀ hn' h2]
  nlinarith [hlog]

/-- A rational upper bound for `log₂ a` from an integer power inequality. -/
lemma logb_two_upper {a m n : ℕ} (ha : 1 < a) (hn : 0 < n) (h : a ^ n < 2 ^ m) :
    Real.logb 2 (a : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) / n := by
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
  have ha' : (1 : ℝ) < a := by exact_mod_cast ha
  have hlt : ((a : ℝ)) ^ n < ((2 : ℝ)) ^ m := by exact_mod_cast h
  have hlog : Real.log ((a : ℝ) ^ n) < Real.log ((2 : ℝ) ^ m) :=
    Real.log_lt_log (by positivity) hlt
  rw [Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow] at hlog
  have hn' : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  rw [Real.logb, div_lt_div_iff₀ h2 hn']
  nlinarith [hlog]

/-- `log₂ 3 > 1054/665`, certified by `2 ^ 1054 < 3 ^ 665`. -/
lemma lb3_lower : (1054 : ℝ) / 665 < Real.logb 2 3 := by
  have h := logb_two_lower (a := 3) (m := 1054) (n := 665) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
    (by decide)
  norm_num at h
  exact h

/-- `log₂ 3 < 485/306`, certified by `3 ^ 306 < 2 ^ 485`. -/

/-! ## 1. Entropy lemmas for constant and factoring read-outs -/

section Generic

variable {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]

/-- A read-out that is constant on `s` has zero entropy. -/
theorem uEnt_eq_zero_of_const {s : Finset α} {g : α → β}
    (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, g x = g y) : uEnt s g = 0 := by
  rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hs
  · simp [uEnt]
  · have hcard : (0 : ℝ) < s.card := by exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 hs
    have hfib : ∀ a ∈ s, ({x ∈ s | g x = g a} : Finset α) = s := fun a ha =>
      Finset.filter_true_of_mem fun x hx => h x hx a ha
    have hsum : ∑ a ∈ s, Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | g x = g a} : ℝ)
        = (s.card : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (s.card : ℝ) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => by rw [hfib a ha]]
      simp [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
    rw [uEnt, hsum, mul_comm, mul_div_assoc, div_self (ne_of_gt hcard), mul_one, sub_self]

/-- If the read-out `g` is a function of the read-out `k`, then conditioning on `k`
annihilates the entropy of `g`. -/
theorem condEnt_eq_zero_of_factors {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} {k : α → γ}
    (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, k x = k y → g x = g y) : condEnt s g k = 0 := by
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun c _ => ?_
  have hz : uEnt {x ∈ s | k x = c} g = 0 := by
    refine uEnt_eq_zero_of_const fun x hx y hy => ?_
    simp only [mem_filter] at hx hy
    exact h x hx.1 y hy.1 (by rw [hx.2, hy.2])
  rw [hz, mul_zero]

/-- **Zero information from a constant read-out.**  A read-out that is constant on the box
carries no information about anything, and hears nothing from anything. -/
theorem mutInfo_eq_zero_of_const {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} (k : α → γ)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, g x = g y) : mutInfo s g k = 0 := by
  have h1 : uEnt s g = 0 := uEnt_eq_zero_of_const h
  have h2 : condEnt s g k = 0 := condEnt_eq_zero_of_factors fun x hx y hy _ => h x hx y hy
  rw [mutInfo, h1, h2, sub_zero]

/-- **Full transmission.**  If the dial `g` is a function of the conditioning read-out `k`,
the information transmitted is the whole entropy of the dial. -/
theorem mutInfo_eq_uEnt_of_factors {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} {k : α → γ}
    (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, k x = k y → g x = g y) : mutInfo s g k = uEnt s g := by
  rw [mutInfo, condEnt_eq_zero_of_factors h, sub_zero]

end Generic

/-! ## 2. The boxes and the read-outs -/

/-- The Chebotarev box of an `S₅` quintic: all `120` Frobenius elements. -/
def S5box : Finset (Perm (Fin 5)) := univ

/-- The Chebotarev box of an `A₅` quintic: the `60` even Frobenius elements. -/
def A5box : Finset (Perm (Fin 5)) := univ.filter fun σ => Perm.sign σ = 1

/-- The splitting type of the quintic at a prime: the cycle type of its Frobenius. -/
def qType (σ : Perm (Fin 5)) : Multiset ℕ := σ.cycleType

/-- The abelianization dial of `S₅`: the sign of the Frobenius, i.e. the quadratic-residue
bit of the discriminant. -/
def signDial (σ : Perm (Fin 5)) : ℤˣ := Perm.sign σ

lemma card_S5box : (#S5box : ℕ) = 120 := by decide

lemma card_A5box : (#A5box : ℕ) = 60 := by decide

lemma mem_A5box {σ : Perm (Fin 5)} : σ ∈ A5box ↔ Perm.sign σ = 1 := by
  rw [A5box, Finset.mem_filter]
  exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨mem_univ _, h⟩⟩

/-- Seven factorisation types occur for an `S₅` quintic: `[1,1,1,1,1]`, `[1,1,1,2]`,
`[1,2,2]`, `[1,1,3]`, `[2,3]`, `[1,4]` and `[5]`. -/
theorem S5_image_qType :
    S5box.image qType = {0, {2}, {2, 2}, {3}, {2, 3}, {4}, {5}} := by decide

/-- Only four factorisation types occur for an `A₅` quintic: the odd types `[1,1,1,2]`,
`[2,3]` and `[1,4]` never occur. -/
theorem A5_image_qType : A5box.image qType = {0, {2, 2}, {3}, {5}} := by decide

theorem S5_card_image_qType : (S5box.image qType).card = 7 := by decide

theorem A5_card_image_qType : (A5box.image qType).card = 4 := by decide

/-! ## 3. The splitting entropies -/

theorem S5_class_sizes :
    (S5box.image qType).val.map (fun v => (#{x ∈ S5box | qType x = v} : ℕ))
      = {1, 10, 15, 20, 20, 30, 24} := by decide

theorem A5_class_sizes :
    (A5box.image qType).val.map (fun v => (#{x ∈ A5box | qType x = v} : ℕ))
      = {1, 15, 20, 24} := by decide

/-- **The `S₅` splitting entropy.**  `H(T) = 7/5 + (17/40) log₂ 3 + (5/24) log₂ 5`. -/
theorem S5_typeEntropy :
    uEnt S5box qType = 7 / 5 + 17 / 40 * Real.logb 2 3 + 5 / 24 * Real.logb 2 5 := by
  rw [uEnt_eq_countSum S5box qType _ S5_class_sizes, card_S5box]
  norm_num [Multiset.insert_eq_cons, lb_120, lb_10, lb_15, lb_20, lb_30, lb_24]
  ring

/-- **The `A₅` splitting entropy.**  `H(T) = 2/15 + (7/20) log₂ 3 + (5/12) log₂ 5`. -/
theorem A5_typeEntropy :
    uEnt A5box qType = 2 / 15 + 7 / 20 * Real.logb 2 3 + 5 / 12 * Real.logb 2 5 := by
  rw [uEnt_eq_countSum A5box qType _ A5_class_sizes, card_A5box]
  norm_num [Multiset.insert_eq_cons, lb_60, lb_15, lb_20, lb_24]
  ring

theorem S5_typeEntropy_bracket :
    2.5573 < uEnt S5box qType ∧ uEnt S5box qType < 2.5574 := by
  rw [S5_typeEntropy]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · nlinarith [lb3_lower, lb5_lower]
  · nlinarith [lb3_upper, lb5_upper]

theorem A5_typeEntropy_bracket :
    1.6555 < uEnt A5box qType ∧ uEnt A5box qType < 1.6556 := by
  rw [A5_typeEntropy]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · nlinarith [lb3_lower, lb5_lower]
  · nlinarith [lb3_upper, lb5_upper]

/-- The `S₅` type channel is strictly richer than the `A₅` one. -/

  have h1 := A5_typeEntropy_bracket.2
  have h2 := S5_typeEntropy_bracket.1
  linarith

/-! ## 4. The abelianization law for `S₅` -/

/-- The sign of a permutation is a function of its cycle type: this is the arithmetic
statement that the quadratic character of the discriminant is readable from the
factorisation type. -/
theorem signDial_of_qType {σ τ : Perm (Fin 5)} (h : qType σ = qType τ) :
    signDial σ = signDial τ := by
  unfold signDial
  rw [Perm.sign_of_cycleType, Perm.sign_of_cycleType]
  unfold qType at h
  rw [h]

lemma sign_fiber_card :
    ∀ σ : Perm (Fin 5), (#{x ∈ S5box | signDial x = signDial σ} : ℕ) = 60 := by decide

/-- The abelianization dial of `S₅` carries exactly one bit. -/
theorem S5_signEntropy : uEnt S5box signDial = 1 := by
  have h := QuinticF20.uEnt_eq_logb_of_uniform_fibers (s := S5box) (g := signDial) (c := 60)
    ⟨1, by simp [S5box]⟩ (fun a _ => sign_fiber_card a)
  rw [h, card_S5box, show ((120 : ℕ) : ℝ) = 2 * ((60 : ℕ) : ℝ) by norm_num]
  exact logb_double (by norm_num)

/-- **The abelianization law at `S₅`.**  The seven-state splitting type transmits exactly one
bit — the quadratic-residue bit of the discriminant — and nothing else. -/
theorem abelianization_law_S5 : mutInfo S5box signDial qType = 1 := by
  rw [mutInfo_eq_uEnt_of_factors (fun x _ y _ h => signDial_of_qType h), S5_signEntropy]

/-! ## 5. The perfection of `A₅` and the two dial theorems -/

/-- An even permutation of five letters. -/
def evenA : Perm (Fin 5) := Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 1 2

/-- A second even permutation, not commuting with `evenA`. -/
def evenB : Perm (Fin 5) := Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 1 3

lemma sign_evenA : Perm.sign evenA = 1 := by decide

lemma sign_evenB : Perm.sign evenB = 1 := by decide

lemma evenA_mul_evenB_ne : evenA * evenB ≠ evenB * evenA := by decide

/-- `A₅` is not commutative. -/
theorem alternating_not_commutative :
    ¬ ∀ x y : alternatingGroup (Fin 5), x * y = y * x := by
  intro h
  have ha : evenA ∈ alternatingGroup (Fin 5) := Perm.mem_alternatingGroup.2 sign_evenA
  have hb : evenB ∈ alternatingGroup (Fin 5) := Perm.mem_alternatingGroup.2 sign_evenB
  exact evenA_mul_evenB_ne (congrArg Subtype.val (h ⟨evenA, ha⟩ ⟨evenB, hb⟩))

/-- **The engine: `A₅` is perfect.**  Every homomorphism from `A₅` into an abelian group is
trivial.  Simplicity forces the kernel to be `⊥` or `⊤`, and `⊥` would make `A₅` abelian. -/
theorem alternating_hom_trivial {M : Type*} [CommGroup M]
    (ψ : alternatingGroup (Fin 5) →* M) (x : alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) : ψ x = 1 := by
  rcases IsSimpleGroup.eq_bot_or_eq_top_of_normal ψ.ker (MonoidHom.normal_ker ψ) with hker | hker
  · exfalso
    have hinj : Function.Injective ψ := (MonoidHom.ker_eq_bot_iff ψ).1 hker
    refine alternating_not_commutative fun a b => hinj ?_
    rw [map_mul, map_mul, mul_comm]
  · have hx : x ∈ ψ.ker := by rw [hker]; exact Subgroup.mem_top x
    exact hx

/-- **The `A₅` seal, pointwise.**  Any multiplicative read-out of the Frobenius into an
abelian group is constant on the `A₅` box. -/
theorem A5_dial_const {M : Type*} [CommGroup M] (d : Perm (Fin 5) → M)
    (hd : ∀ x ∈ A5box, ∀ y ∈ A5box, d (x * y) = d x * d y)
    {x y : Perm (Fin 5)} (hx : x ∈ A5box) (hy : y ∈ A5box) : d x = d y := by
  have hmul : ∀ a b : alternatingGroup (Fin 5),
      d ((a * b : alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) : Perm (Fin 5)) = d (a : Perm (Fin 5)) * d b :=
    fun a b => hd a (mem_A5box.2 (Perm.mem_alternatingGroup.1 a.2)) b
      (mem_A5box.2 (Perm.mem_alternatingGroup.1 b.2))
  let ψ : alternatingGroup (Fin 5) →* M :=
    { toFun := fun a => d (a : Perm (Fin 5))
      map_one' := by
        have h := hmul 1 1
        simp only [mul_one, OneMemClass.coe_one] at h
        have h' : d 1 * 1 = d 1 * d 1 := by rw [mul_one]; exact h
        exact (mul_left_cancel h').symm
      map_mul' := hmul }
  have hx' : x ∈ alternatingGroup (Fin 5) := Perm.mem_alternatingGroup.2 (mem_A5box.1 hx)
  have hy' : y ∈ alternatingGroup (Fin 5) := Perm.mem_alternatingGroup.2 (mem_A5box.1 hy)
  have h1 : ψ ⟨x, hx'⟩ = 1 := alternating_hom_trivial ψ _
  have h2 : ψ ⟨y, hy'⟩ = 1 := alternating_hom_trivial ψ _
  simpa [ψ] using h1.trans h2.symm

/-- **The complete seal of the `A₅` type channel.**  No abelian (residue) dial can hear
anything about *any* read-out of the Frobenius, nor be heard by it: the mutual information is
exactly `0`, with no parameter to tune. -/
theorem A5_seal {M : Type*} [CommGroup M] [DecidableEq M] {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (d : Perm (Fin 5) → M) (T : Perm (Fin 5) → β)
    (hd : ∀ x ∈ A5box, ∀ y ∈ A5box, d (x * y) = d x * d y) :

  linarith [condEnt_nonneg s g k]

/-! ## 3. The group form: `G^ab = C₂` gives exactly one bit

the abelian quotient; when that quotient has order two, the visible datum is a single surjective
character `χ : G →* C` with `|C| = 2`, and the splitting type determines it. -/

section GroupForm

/-- The canonical map to the abelianization is surjective. -/
theorem abelianization_of_surjective {G : Type*} [Group G] :
    Function.Surjective (Abelianization.of : G → Abelianization G) := by
  intro x
  induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
  | H g => exact ⟨g, rfl⟩

variable {G C : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [Group C] [Fintype C] [DecidableEq C]

/-- Every fibre of a surjective character onto a two-element group is exactly half of the group. -/
theorem card_fiber_character (χ : G →* C) (hsurj : Function.Surjective χ)
    (hC : Fintype.card C = 2) (a : G) :
    2 * #{x : G | χ x = χ a} = Fintype.card G := by
  classical
  have hsum : Fintype.card G = ∑ c : C, #{x : G | χ x = c} :=
    Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (fun x _ => Finset.mem_univ (χ x))
  have hconst : ∀ c : C, #{x : G | χ x = c} = #{x : G | χ x = χ a} :=
    fun c => MonoidHom.card_fiber_eq_of_mem_range χ (hsurj c) ⟨a, rfl⟩
  rw [hsum, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => hconst c, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, hC,
    smul_eq_mul]

/-- **`G^ab = C₂` ⟹ exactly one bit.**  For any finite group `G`, any surjective character
`χ : G →* C` onto a two-element group, and any splitting-type read-out `T` through which `χ`
factors, the type/character channel carries exactly one bit.  Nothing about `G` beyond the
existence of the index-two kernel is used — this is the promised uniformity over all `S₃`, `S₄`
and `S₅` fields. -/
theorem mutInfo_character_eq_one {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β] (T : G → β) (χ : G →* C)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective χ) (hC : Fintype.card C = 2)
    (f : β → C) (hf : ∀ x : G, χ x = f (T x)) :
    mutInfo (univ : Finset G) T (fun x => χ x) = 1 := by
  classical
  have hne : (univ : Finset G).Nonempty := univ_nonempty
  refine mutInfo_eq_one_of_refines_balanced hne (fun x _ y _ hxy => ?_) (fun a _ => ?_)
  · rw [hf x, hf y, hxy]
  · rw [Finset.card_univ]
    exact card_fiber_character χ hsurj hC a

/-- The same statement with the abelianization in place of an abstract character: if `G^ab` has
order two and the type read-out determines the image in `G^ab`, the channel is one bit. -/
theorem mutInfo_abelianization_eq_one {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype (Abelianization G)] [DecidableEq (Abelianization G)]
    (T : G → β) (hC : Fintype.card (Abelianization G) = 2)
    (f : β → Abelianization G) (hf : ∀ x : G, Abelianization.of x = f (T x)) :
    mutInfo (univ : Finset G) T (fun x => Abelianization.of x) = 1 :=
  mutInfo_character_eq_one T (Abelianization.of) abelianization_of_surjective hC f hf

end GroupForm

def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> CycleType:
    """Cycle type of a permutation, as a sorted tuple of cycle lengths."""
    n = len(p)
    seen = [False] * n
    lengths: List[int] = []
    for i in range(n):
        if not seen[i]:
            ell, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                ell += 1
            lengths.append(ell)
    return tuple(sorted(lengths))


def sign_of(p: Perm) -> int:
    """Sign of a permutation: +1 for even, -1 for odd."""
    s = 1
    for ell in cycle_type(p):
        if ell % 2 == 0:
            s = -s
    return s


def compose(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    """Composition (p after q)."""
    return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(len(q)))

def entropy_of_counts(counts: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """Shannon entropy in bits of an empirical histogram."""
    c = [x for x in counts if x > 0]
    n = sum(c)
    return -sum((x / n) * log2(x / n) for x in c)


def entropy(box: Sequence[object], f: Callable[[object], object]) -> float:
    """H(f) for the uniform (counting) measure on `box`."""
    counts: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for x in box:
        counts[f(x)] = counts.get(f(x), 0) + 1
    return entropy_of_counts(counts.values())


def cond_entropy(box: Sequence[object],
                 f: Callable[[object], object],
                 g: Callable[[object], object]) -> float:
    """H(f | g) for the uniform measure on `box`."""
    strata: Dict[object, List[object]] = {}
    for x in box:
        strata.setdefault(g(x), []).append(x)
    n = len(box)
    return sum(len(s) / n * entropy(s, f) for s in strata.values())


def mutual_info(box: Sequence[object],

                g: Callable[[object], object]) -> float:
    """I(f ; g) = H(f) - H(f | g)."""
    return entropy(box, f) - cond_entropy(box, f, g)

    print("    A5, k = 2 (semiprime seal):  I =",

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Arithmetic: factorisation types of quintics mod p
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

Poly = List[int]  # little-endian coefficient list over F_p


def poly_trim(a: Poly) -> Poly:
    while a and a[-1] == 0:
        a.pop()
    return a


def poly_mul(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    if not a or not b:
        return []
    out = [0] * (len(a) + len(b) - 1)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        if ai:
            for j, bj in enumerate(b):
                out[i + j] = (out[i + j] + ai * bj) % p
    return poly_trim(out)


def poly_divmod(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Tuple[Poly, Poly]:
    a = a[:]
    db = len(b) - 1
    inv = pow(b[-1], p - 2, p)
    q = [0] * max(0, len(a) - db)
    while len(a) - 1 >= db and a:
        shift = len(a) - 1 - db
        c = (a[-1] * inv) % p
        q[shift] = c
        for i, bi in enumerate(b):
            a[shift + i] = (a[shift + i] - c * bi) % p
        poly_trim(a)
    return poly_trim(q), a


def poly_gcd(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a, b = poly_trim(a[:]), poly_trim(b[:])
    while b:
        a, b = b, poly_divmod(a, b, p)[1]
    if a:
        inv = pow(a[-1], p - 2, p)
        a = [(c * inv) % p for c in a]
    return a


def poly_powmod(base: Poly, e: int, mod: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    result: Poly = [1]
    b = poly_divmod(base, mod, p)[1]
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            result = poly_divmod(poly_mul(result, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        b = poly_divmod(poly_mul(b, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        e >>= 1
    return result


def poly_sub(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    n = max(len(a), len(b))
    out = [((a[i] if i < len(a) else 0) - (b[i] if i < len(b) else 0)) % p
           for i in range(n)]
    return poly_trim(out)


def factorisation_type(f: Poly, p: int) -> CycleType | None:
    """
    Degrees of the irreducible factors of a squarefree f over F_p, sorted.
    Returns None if f is not squarefree mod p (a ramified prime).
    """
    f = poly_trim([c % p for c in f])
    df = poly_trim([(i * f[i]) % p for i in range(1, len(f))])
    if not df or len(poly_gcd(f, df, p)) > 1:
        return None
    degrees: List[int] = []
    h: Poly = [0, 1]                      # x
    g = f[:]
    d = 0
    while len(g) - 1 > 0 and d < len(f):
        d += 1
        h = poly_powmod(h, p, g, p)       # x^(p^d) mod g
        gd = poly_gcd(g, poly_sub(h, [0, 1], p), p)
        if len(gd) - 1 > 0:
            # gd is a product of (deg gd)/d irreducibles, each of degree d
            degrees.extend([d] * ((len(gd) - 1) // d))
            g = poly_divmod(g, gd, p)[0]
            h = poly_divmod(h, g, p)[1] if len(g) - 1 > 0 else h
    if len(g) - 1 > 0:
        degrees.append(len(g) - 1)
    return tuple(sorted(degrees))


def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i:: i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i:: i]))
    return [i for i in range(2, n + 1) if sieve[i]]


def kronecker_symbol(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    """Legendre symbol (a/p) for odd prime p."""
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    return 1 if pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p) == 1 else -1


def part_three_arithmetic(limit: int = 60000) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print("3.  ARITHMETIC REALISATION: FACTORISATION TYPES OF QUINTICS MOD p")
    print("=" * 74)

    f_S5: Poly = [-1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 1]      # x^5 - x - 1,  disc = 2869 = 19 * 151
    f_A5: Poly = [16, 20, 0, 0, 0, 1]      # x^5 + 20x + 16, disc a perfect square

    primes = primes_up_to(limit)
    print(f"  using {len(primes)} primes below {limit}")

    for name, f, box in (("x^5 - x - 1   (S5)", f_S5, S5),
                         ("x^5 + 20x + 16 (A5)", f_A5, A5)):
        data: List[Tuple[int, CycleType]] = []
        for p in primes:
            t = factorisation_type(f, p)
            if t is not None and sum(t) == 5:
                data.append((p, t))
        counts: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
        for _, t in data:
            counts[t] = counts.get(t, 0) + 1
        gcounts: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
        for s in box:
            gcounts[cycle_type(s)] = gcounts.get(cycle_type(s), 0) + 1

        print(f"\n  {name}:  {len(data)} unramified primes")
        worst = 0.0
        for t in sorted(gcounts, key=lambda t: (len(t), t)):
            obs = counts.get(t, 0) / len(data)
            pred = gcounts[t] / len(box)
            worst = max(worst, abs(obs - pred))
            print(f"      type {str(list(t)):<16} observed {obs:.4f}   Chebotarev {pred:.4f}")
        extra = set(counts) - set(gcounts)
        print(f"      largest deviation from the predicted density: {worst:.4f}")
        if extra:
            print(f"      UNEXPECTED types observed: {sorted(extra)}")
        else:
            print("      no unexpected type ever occurs")
        print(f"      empirical H(T) = {entropy_of_counts(counts.values()):.4f} bits"
              f"   (group value {entropy(box, cycle_type):.4f})")


def part_four_permutation_reference(limit: int = 200000, shuffles: int = 200) -> None:
    """
    The measurement discipline: the plug-in estimate of I(residue ; type) at a
    large conductor is biased upward simply because the residue dial has many
    classes.  The honest comparison is against a permutation reference that
    preserves exactly the channel the law predicts (here: the sign stratum)
    and randomises only the finer assignment.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print("4.  PERMUTATION-REFERENCED MEASUREMENT OF THE RESIDUE CHANNEL")
    print("=" * 74)
    random.seed(20240917)

    f_S5: Poly = [-1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 1]
    f_A5: Poly = [16, 20, 0, 0, 0, 1]
    disc_S5 = 2869                                # = 19 * 151

    primes = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if p > 5]

    # --- S5: the sign agreement, exact by the abelianization law -------------
    rows: List[Tuple[int, CycleType]] = []
    for p in primes:
        if disc_S5 % p == 0:
            continue
        t = factorisation_type(f_S5, p)
        if t is not None and sum(t) == 5:
            rows.append((p, t))

    def type_parity(t: CycleType) -> int:
        s = 1
        for ell in t:
            if ell % 2 == 0:
                s = -s
        return s

    agree = sum(1 for p, t in rows if type_parity(t) == kronecker_symbol(disc_S5, p))
    print(f"  S5: parity of the factorisation type vs the quadratic character of the")
    print(f"      discriminant 2869 = 19 * 151 :  agreement = {agree / len(rows):.4f}"
          f"   over {len(rows)} primes")
    print("      (an exact 0.0000 or 1.0000 is the signature of a correct law;"
          " anything in between would flag a bug)")

    # --- the plug-in bias of the residue dial and its permutation reference --
    resid = [p % disc_S5 for p, _ in rows]
    types = [t for _, t in rows]
    signs = [type_parity(t) for t in types]
    box = list(range(len(rows)))
    I_raw = mutual_info(box, lambda i: resid[i], lambda i: types[i])

    null_values: List[float] = []
    for _ in range(shuffles):
        # permute the residues WITHIN each sign stratum: this preserves the one
        # bit the law predicts and randomises only the finer assignment
        by_sign: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
        for i in box:
            by_sign.setdefault(signs[i], []).append(i)
        shuffled = resid[:]
        for s, idxs in by_sign.items():
            vals = [resid[i] for i in idxs]
            random.shuffle(vals)
            for i, v in zip(idxs, vals):
                shuffled[i] = v
        null_values.append(mutual_info(box, lambda i: shuffled[i], lambda i: types[i]))

    mu = sum(null_values) / len(null_values)
    var = sum((v - mu) ** 2 for v in null_values) / (len(null_values) - 1)
    sd = var ** 0.5
    z = (I_raw - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0
    print(f"\n      raw plug-in  I(p mod 2869 ; T) = {I_raw:.4f} bits")
    print(f"      permutation reference          = {mu:.4f} +- {sd:.4f}")
    print(f"      z = {z:+.2f}   -> the excess over the law's exactly 1 bit is plug-in bias,")
    print("      not extra signal: the channel really carries one bit and no more")

    # --- A5: the seal, measured -------------------------------------------
    rowsA: List[Tuple[int, CycleType]] = []
    for p in primes:
        t = factorisation_type(f_A5, p)
        if t is not None and sum(t) == 5:
            rowsA.append((p, t))
    print(f"\n  A5: {len(rowsA)} unramified primes, "
          f"{len(set(t for _, t in rowsA))} distinct types observed")
    boxA = list(range(len(rowsA)))
    typesA = [t for _, t in rowsA]
    worst_z = 0.0
    for m in (3, 7, 11, 31):
        res = [p % m for p, _ in rowsA]
        I_raw = mutual_info(boxA, lambda i: res[i], lambda i: typesA[i])
        nulls: List[float] = []
        for _ in range(shuffles):
            sh = res[:]
            random.shuffle(sh)
            nulls.append(mutual_info(boxA, lambda i: sh[i], lambda i: typesA[i]))
        mu = sum(nulls) / len(nulls)
        sd = (sum((v - mu) ** 2 for v in nulls) / (len(nulls) - 1)) ** 0.5
        z = (I_raw - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0
        worst_z = max(worst_z, abs(z))
        print(f"      m = {m:>2}:  I = {I_raw:.4f},  null = {mu:.4f} +- {sd:.4f},  z = {z:+.2f}")
    print(f"      largest |z| over the four moduli: {worst_z:.2f}")
    print("      every direction sits at its own permutation null, and the raw values are three")
    print("      orders of magnitude below the 1.6555 bits of splitting entropy present: the")
    print("      four-state type channel of a perfect group is sealed, with nothing tuned")


def main() -> None:
    part_one_group_theory()
    part_two_dials()
    part_three_arithmetic()
    part_four_permutation_reference()
    print("\nall demonstrations complete.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> CycleType:
    seen = [False] * len(p)
    out: List[int] = []
    for i in range(len(p)):
        if not seen[i]:
            ell, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                ell += 1
            out.append(ell)
    return tuple(sorted(out))

    return s

    out: Dict[object, int] = {}

def entropy(counts: Dict[object, int]) -> float:
    n = sum(counts.values())
    return -sum((c / n) * log2(c / n) for c in counts.values() if c > 0)

    def product_channel(box: List[Perm], dial, mul, unit, k: int) -> float:

        for x in box:

            d = by_type[cycle_type(x)]

                 {v: c / sum(d.values()) for v, c in d.items()})
                for d in by_type.values()]

        def conv(a: Dict[object, float], b: Dict[object, float]) -> Dict[object, float]:
            out: Dict[object, float] = {}
            for u, pu in a.items():
                for v, pv in b.items():
                    w = mul(u, v)
                    out[w] = out.get(w, 0.0) + pu * pv
            return out

            return -sum(p * log2(p) for p in d.values() if p > 0)

        marg: Dict[object, float] = {}
        for x in box:
            marg[dial(x)] = marg.get(dial(x), 0.0) + 1 / len(box)
        mk: Dict[object, float] = {unit: 1.0}
        for _ in range(k):

        cond = 0.0
        m = len(rows)

        def walk(i: int, left: int, weight: float, dist: Dict[object, float],

            if i == m - 1:

                for _ in range(c):
                    d = conv(d, rows[i][1])
                walk(i + 1, left - c, weight * rows[i][0] ** c, d, counts + [c])

        walk(0, k, 1.0, {unit: 1.0}, [])
        return ent(mk) - cond

",
    "algorithm_splitting_type_census": """"
Frobenius splitting-type census by distinct-degree factorisation.

For a monic integer polynomial f of degree n and every prime p below a bound,
the algorithm computes the degree pattern of f mod p -- equivalently, by
Dedekind's theorem, the cycle type of the Frobenius element of p -- and returns
the empirical histogram of types together with its entropy.

Method.  Over F_p the polynomial x^(p^d) - x is the product of all monic
irreducibles whose degree divides d.  Repeatedly computing
g_d = gcd(f_d, x^(p^d) - x) and dividing it out therefore peels off, for
d = 1, 2, ..., the product of all irreducible factors of degree exactly d; the
number of them is deg(g_d)/d.  A non-trivial gcd of f with f' detects a
ramified prime, which is skipped.

Complexity.  For each prime, O(n^2 log p) operations in F_p for the repeated
squaring plus O(n^2) per gcd, i.e. O(pi(X) n^2 log X) in total.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from math import log2
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

Poly = List[int]          # little-endian coefficients over F_p
CycleType = Tuple[int, ...]


def trim(a: Poly) -> Poly:
    while a and a[-1] == 0:
        a.pop()
    return a


def mul(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    if not a or not b:
        return []
    out = [0] * (len(a) + len(b) - 1)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        if ai:
            for j, bj in enumerate(b):
                out[i + j] = (out[i + j] + ai * bj) % p
    return trim(out)


def divmod_(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Tuple[Poly, Poly]:
    a, db = a[:], len(b) - 1
    inv = pow(b[-1], p - 2, p)
    q = [0] * max(0, len(a) - db)
    while a and len(a) - 1 >= db:
        shift = len(a) - 1 - db
        c = (a[-1] * inv) % p
        q[shift] = c
        for i, bi in enumerate(b):
            a[shift + i] = (a[shift + i] - c * bi) % p
        trim(a)
    return trim(q), a


def gcd_(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a, b = trim(a[:]), trim(b[:])
    while b:
        a, b = b, divmod_(a, b, p)[1]
    if a:
        inv = pow(a[-1], p - 2, p)
        a = [(c * inv) % p for c in a]
    return a


def powmod(base: Poly, e: int, mod: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    r: Poly = [1]
    b = divmod_(base, mod, p)[1]
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            r = divmod_(mul(r, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        b = divmod_(mul(b, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        e >>= 1
    return r


def sub(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    n = max(len(a), len(b))
    return trim([((a[i] if i < len(a) else 0) - (b[i] if i < len(b) else 0)) % p
                 for i in range(n)])


def splitting_type(f: Poly, p: int) -> Optional[CycleType]:
    """Degree pattern of f mod p, or None if p is ramified for f."""
    f = trim([c % p for c in f])
    df = trim([(i * f[i]) % p for i in range(1, len(f))])
    if not df or len(gcd_(f, df, p)) > 1:
        return None
    degrees: List[int] = []
    h: Poly = [0, 1]                       # x
    g, d = f[:], 0
    while len(g) - 1 > 0 and d < len(f):
        d += 1
        h = powmod(h, p, g, p)             # x^(p^d) mod g
        gd = gcd_(g, sub(h, [0, 1], p), p)
        if len(gd) - 1 > 0:
            degrees.extend([d] * ((len(gd) - 1) // d))
            g = divmod_(g, gd, p)[0]
            if len(g) - 1 > 0:
                h = divmod_(h, g, p)[1]
    if len(g) - 1 > 0:
        degrees.append(len(g) - 1)
    return tuple(sorted(degrees))


def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i:: i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i:: i]))
    return [i for i in range(2, n + 1) if sieve[i]]


def census(f: Poly, limit: int) -> Tuple[Dict[CycleType, int], List[int], float]:
    """Histogram of splitting types, list of ramified primes, and entropy in bits."""
    hist: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
    ramified: List[int] = []
    for p in primes_up_to(limit):
        t = splitting_type(f, p)
        if t is None:
            ramified.append(p)
        else:
            hist[t] = hist.get(t, 0) + 1
    total = sum(hist.values())
    h = -sum((c / total) * log2(c / total) for c in hist.values())
    return hist, ramified, h


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name, f in (("x^5 - x - 1", [-1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 1]),
                    ("x^5 + 20x + 16", [16, 20, 0, 0, 0, 1])):
        hist, ram, h = census(f, 20000)
        total = sum(hist.values())
        print(f"\n{name}:  {total} unramified primes,  ramified primes {ram}")
        for t, c in sorted(hist.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            print(f"   type {str(list(t)):<16} {c:>5}   density {c/total:.4f}")
        print(f"   empirical splitting entropy H(T) = {h:.4f} bits")
",
    "algorithm_permutation_reference": """"
Permutation-referenced estimation of the residue-to-type channel.

The plug-in ("count and divide") estimator of mutual information is biased
upward, and the bias grows with the number of classes of the conditioning
variable.  At a conductor such as 2869 the residue dial has 2868 classes, so a
few thousand primes produce an apparent excess of a fifth of a bit out of pure
sparsity.  The remedy is a permutation reference designed so that

    * the channel the theory predicts is PRESERVED, and
    * only the finer assignment is randomised.

Concretely, one permutes the residues WITHIN each stratum of the predicted
channel (here: the parity of the splitting type).  Any estimate that lands on
the resulting null distribution is fully explained by the predicted channel
plus estimator bias.

Complexity: O(N) per estimate and O(S * N) for S shuffles, with N the number of
primes; memory O(N + number of classes).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from math import log2
from typing import Dict, Hashable, List, Sequence, Tuple


def mutual_information(xs: Sequence[Hashable], ys: Sequence[Hashable]) -> float:
    """Plug-in estimate of I(X ; Y) in bits from paired samples."""
    n = len(xs)
    px: Dict[Hashable, int] = {}
    py: Dict[Hashable, int] = {}
    pxy: Dict[Tuple[Hashable, Hashable], int] = {}
    for a, b in zip(xs, ys):
        px[a] = px.get(a, 0) + 1
        py[b] = py.get(b, 0) + 1
        pxy[(a, b)] = pxy.get((a, b), 0) + 1
    ent = lambda d: -sum((c / n) * log2(c / n) for c in d.values())
    return ent(px) + ent(py) - ent(pxy)


def stratified_permutation_null(xs: Sequence[Hashable],
                                ys: Sequence[Hashable],
                                strata: Sequence[Hashable],
                                shuffles: int = 200,
                                seed: int = 0) -> Tuple[float, float, List[float]]:
    """
    Mean, standard deviation and raw values of the permutation reference obtained
    by permuting the X-values within each stratum.  The strata must be the channel
    the theory predicts (so it survives the shuffle); everything finer is destroyed.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    index: Dict[Hashable, List[int]] = {}
    for i, s in enumerate(strata):
        index.setdefault(s, []).append(i)
    values: List[float] = []
    for _ in range(shuffles):
        shuffled = list(xs)
        for idxs in index.values():
            pool = [xs[i] for i in idxs]
            rng.shuffle(pool)
            for i, v in zip(idxs, pool):
                shuffled[i] = v
        values.append(mutual_information(shuffled, ys))
    mu = sum(values) / len(values)
    sd = (sum((v - mu) ** 2 for v in values) / (len(values) - 1)) ** 0.5
    return mu, sd, values


def referenced_estimate(xs: Sequence[Hashable],
                        ys: Sequence[Hashable],
                        strata: Sequence[Hashable],
                        shuffles: int = 200,
                        seed: int = 0) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Raw plug-in estimate together with its permutation reference and z-score."""
    raw = mutual_information(xs, ys)
    mu, sd, _ = stratified_permutation_null(xs, ys, strata, shuffles, seed)
    return {"raw": raw, "null_mean": mu, "null_sd": sd,
            "z": (raw - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0, "bias": mu}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # A synthetic illustration of the bias: a dial with many classes that is
    # correlated with the read-out through exactly one bit and nothing else.
    rng = random.Random(1)
    n, conductor = 6000, 2869
    types = ["even-A", "even-B", "odd-A", "odd-B"]
    ys: List[str] = []
    xs: List[int] = []
    strata: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.choice(types)
        ys.append(t)
        par = "even" if t.startswith("even") else "odd"
        strata.append(par)
        # the residue carries the parity bit exactly, and nothing finer
        r = rng.randrange(conductor)
        if (r % 2 == 0) != (par == "even"):
            r = (r + 1) % conductor
        xs.append(r)
    out = referenced_estimate(xs, ys, strata, shuffles=100, seed=7)
    print(f"raw plug-in estimate : {out['raw']:.4f} bits   (truth: 1 bit)")
    print(f"permutation reference: {out['null_mean']:.4f} +- {out['null_sd']:.4f}")
    print(f"z = {out['z']:+.2f}  -> the excess over 1 bit is estimator bias, not signal")

    "algorithm_channel_capacity": """"
Exact capacity of the congruence channel of a Galois group.

Given a finite group G (here realised as a permutation group on the roots of a
quintic), the algorithm returns:

    * the splitting entropy H(T)  of the cycle-type read-out,
    * the abelianization ceiling  log2 |G / [G,G]|,
    * the information I(dial ; T) actually transmitted by the universal dial
      G -> G/[G,G], and
    * whether the ceiling is attained, i.e. whether the cycle type determines
      the dial value.

Complexity: O(|G|^2) group operations for the commutator generators, plus
O(|D| * |G|) for the coset labelling, where D = [G,G]; entropies are O(|G|).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations
from math import log2
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


def compose(p: Perm, q: Perm) -> Perm:
    return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(len(q)))


def inverse(p: Perm) -> Perm:
    r = [0] * len(p)
    for i, v in enumerate(p):
        r[v] = i
    return tuple(r)


def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    seen = [False] * len(p)
    out: List[int] = []
    for i in range(len(p)):
        if not seen[i]:
            ell, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                ell += 1
            out.append(ell)
    return tuple(sorted(out))


def derived_subgroup(G: List[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """The commutator subgroup [G, G], by closure of the commutator generators."""
    ident = tuple(range(len(G[0])))
    elems = {ident}
    for x in G:
        for y in G:
            elems.add(compose(compose(x, y), compose(inverse(x), inverse(y))))
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for x in list(elems):
            for y in list(elems):
                z = compose(x, y)
                if z not in elems:
                    elems.add(z)
                    changed = True
    return sorted(elems)


def entropy(counts: Dict[object, int]) -> float:
    n = sum(counts.values())
    return -sum((c / n) * log2(c / n) for c in counts.values() if c > 0)


def channel_capacity(G: List[Perm]) -> Dict[str, object]:
    D = derived_subgroup(G)
    label = {x: min(compose(x, d) for d in D) for x in G}

    tcount: Dict[object, int] = {}
    dcount: Dict[object, int] = {}
    jcount: Dict[object, int] = {}
    for x in G:
        t, d = cycle_type(x), label[x]
        tcount[t] = tcount.get(t, 0) + 1
        dcount[d] = dcount.get(d, 0) + 1
        jcount[(t, d)] = jcount.get((t, d), 0) + 1

    h_t, h_d, h_j = entropy(tcount), entropy(dcount), entropy(jcount)
    mi = h_t + h_d - h_j
    ceiling = log2(len(G) / len(D))
    refines = len({t for (t, _) in jcount}) == len(jcount)
    return {
        "order": len(G),
        "abelianization_order": len(G) // len(D),
        "num_types": len(tcount),
        "H_T": h_t,
        "H_dial": h_d,
        "I_dial_T": mi,
        "ceiling": ceiling,
        "ceiling_attained": abs(mi - ceiling) < 1e-12,
        "type_determines_dial": refines,
    }


def transitive_quintic_groups() -> Dict[str, List[Perm]]:
    allp = [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(5))]

    def sign(p: Perm) -> int:
        s = 1
        for ell in cycle_type(p):
            if ell % 2 == 0:
                s = -s
        return s

    aff = lambda a, b: tuple((a * x + b) % 5 for x in range(5))
    return {
        "C5": [aff(1, b) for b in range(5)],
        "D5": [aff(a, b) for a in (1, 4) for b in range(5)],
        "F20": [aff(a, b) for a in (1, 2, 3, 4) for b in range(5)],
        "A5": [p for p in allp if sign(p) == 1],
        "S5": allp,
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"{'group':>5} {'|G|':>4} {'|Gab|':>5} {'#T':>3} {'H(T)':>8} {'I':>8} {'cap':>8}  attained")
    for name, G in transitive_quintic_groups().items():
        r = channel_capacity(G)
        print(f"{name:>5} {r['order']:>4} {r['abelianization_order']:>5} {r['num_types']:>3} "
              f"{r['H_T']:>8.4f} {r['I_dial_T']:>8.4f} {r['ceiling']:>8.4f}  {r['ceiling_attained']}")

Visualisation: the degree-five splitting-type channel at its two extremes.

Panel 1  Splitting-type densities for S5 and A5 quintics: the exact Chebotarev
         densities (bars) against the observed frequencies of the factorisation
         types of x^5 - x - 1 and x^5 + 20x + 16 over the primes below 30000
         (dots).  The three odd types are structurally absent for A5.
Panel 2  The bit ledger across the transitive quintic groups: total splitting

Requires matplotlib.  Run:  python3 viz_channel_ledger.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations
from math import log2
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]
CycleType = Tuple[int, ...]


def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> CycleType:
    seen = [False] * len(p)
    out: List[int] = []
    for i in range(len(p)):
        if not seen[i]:
            ell, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                ell += 1
            out.append(ell)
    return tuple(sorted(out))


def sign_of(p: Perm) -> int:
    s = 1
    for ell in cycle_type(p):
        if ell % 2 == 0:
            s = -s
    return s


S5: List[Perm] = [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(5))]
A5: List[Perm] = [p for p in S5 if sign_of(p) == 1]
F20: List[Perm] = [tuple((a * x + b) % 5 for x in range(5))
                   for a in (1, 2, 3, 4) for b in range(5)]
D5: List[Perm] = [tuple((a * x + b) % 5 for x in range(5))
                  for a in (1, 4) for b in range(5)]
C5: List[Perm] = [tuple((x + b) % 5 for x in range(5)) for b in range(5)]


def densities(box: List[Perm]) -> Dict[CycleType, float]:
    counts: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
    for p in box:
        counts[cycle_type(p)] = counts.get(cycle_type(p), 0) + 1
    return {t: c / len(box) for t, c in counts.items()}


def entropy(dist: Dict[CycleType, float]) -> float:
    return -sum(q * log2(q) for q in dist.values() if q > 0)


# --- observed factorisation types of the two quintics -------------------------

def primes_up_to(n: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i:: i] = bytearray(len(sieve[i * i:: i]))
    return [i for i in range(2, n + 1) if sieve[i]]


Poly = List[int]


def _trim(a: Poly) -> Poly:
    while a and a[-1] == 0:
        a.pop()
    return a


def _mul(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    if not a or not b:
        return []
    out = [0] * (len(a) + len(b) - 1)
    for i, ai in enumerate(a):
        if ai:
            for j, bj in enumerate(b):
                out[i + j] = (out[i + j] + ai * bj) % p
    return _trim(out)


def _divmod(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Tuple[Poly, Poly]:
    a, db = a[:], len(b) - 1
    inv = pow(b[-1], p - 2, p)
    q = [0] * max(0, len(a) - db)
    while a and len(a) - 1 >= db:
        shift = len(a) - 1 - db
        c = (a[-1] * inv) % p
        q[shift] = c
        for i, bi in enumerate(b):
            a[shift + i] = (a[shift + i] - c * bi) % p
        _trim(a)
    return _trim(q), a


def _gcd(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    a, b = _trim(a[:]), _trim(b[:])
    while b:
        a, b = b, _divmod(a, b, p)[1]
    if a:
        inv = pow(a[-1], p - 2, p)
        a = [(c * inv) % p for c in a]
    return a


def _powmod(base: Poly, e: int, mod: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    r: Poly = [1]
    b = _divmod(base, mod, p)[1]
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            r = _divmod(_mul(r, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        b = _divmod(_mul(b, b, p), mod, p)[1]
        e >>= 1
    return r


def _sub(a: Poly, b: Poly, p: int) -> Poly:
    n = max(len(a), len(b))
    return _trim([((a[i] if i < len(a) else 0) - (b[i] if i < len(b) else 0)) % p
                  for i in range(n)])


def factorisation_type(f: Poly, p: int):
    f = _trim([c % p for c in f])
    df = _trim([(i * f[i]) % p for i in range(1, len(f))])
    if not df or len(_gcd(f, df, p)) > 1:
        return None
    degrees: List[int] = []
    h: Poly = [0, 1]
    g, d = f[:], 0
    while len(g) - 1 > 0 and d < len(f):
        d += 1
        h = _powmod(h, p, g, p)
        gd = _gcd(g, _sub(h, [0, 1], p), p)
        if len(gd) - 1 > 0:
            degrees.extend([d] * ((len(gd) - 1) // d))
            g = _divmod(g, gd, p)[0]
            if len(g) - 1 > 0:
                h = _divmod(h, g, p)[1]
    if len(g) - 1 > 0:
        degrees.append(len(g) - 1)
    return tuple(sorted(degrees))


def observed(f: Poly, limit: int = 30000) -> Dict[CycleType, float]:
    counts: Dict[CycleType, int] = {}
    total = 0
    for p in primes_up_to(limit):
        t = factorisation_type(f, p)
        if t is not None and sum(t) == 5:
            counts[t] = counts.get(t, 0) + 1
            total += 1
    return {t: c / total for t, c in counts.items()}


def main() -> None:

    labels = ["[1,1,1,1,1]", "[1,1,1,2]", "[1,2,2]", "[1,1,3]", "[2,3]", "[1,4]", "[5]"]

    ax.plot([x - w / 2 for x in xs], [oS.get(t, 0) for t in order], "o",

    ax.plot([x + w / 2 for x in xs], [oA.get(t, 0) for t in order], "s",

    ax.set_xticks(list(xs))

    ax.set_title("Splitting types: prediction vs. observation\n"

    ax.legend(fontsize=9)

    groups = [("$C_5$", C5, log2(5)), ("$D_5$", D5, 1.0), ("$F_{20}$", F20, 2.0),

    xs = range(len(groups))

    ax.bar([x for x in xs], heard, width=0.26, color="#ffa657", label="I(dial ; T): heard by a congruence")
